Level: level-2b (6 challenges)

lvl2b_2mlh9o variant: checker-shadow target: N/A
Are squares A and B the same shade?
Ground Truth Answer:
Yes
Squares A and B have identical physical luminance and RGB reflectance. The perceptual shadow context creates an illusion of different shades.
lvl2b_4oq84p variant: checker-shadow target: N/A
Are horizontal bars A and B the same length?
Ground Truth Answer:
Yes
Both yellow horizontal bars are exactly 130 pixels long. The linear perspective created by the converging rails induces an illusion that Bar A is larger.
lvl2b_7c5cth variant: checker-shadow target: N/A
Are the horizontal mortar lines dividing the rows parallel?
Ground Truth Answer:
Yes
Every horizontal grey mortar line is perfectly horizontal and parallel (slope = 0.0). The staggered black and white tiles create luminance border-locking signals that mislead human edge detectors.
lvl2b_90aspy variant: checker-shadow target: N/A
Are the two orange center circles the same size?
Ground Truth Answer:
Yes
Both central orange circles have an identical diameter of 60 pixels. The size contrast of the surrounding inducers causes Circle A to appear smaller than Circle B.
lvl2b_m73rcm variant: checker-shadow target: N/A
Are squares A and B the same shade of grey?
Ground Truth Answer:
Yes
Both Square A and Square B have the exact same RGB color (130, 130, 130). Lateral inhibition causes Square A to appear significantly lighter against its dark surround.
lvl2b_w8fc0h variant: checker-shadow target: N/A
Are horizontal lines A and B the same length?
Ground Truth Answer:
Yes
Both central horizontal line shafts are exactly 260 pixels long. The inward vs outward orientation of the tail fins produces a powerful perceptual illusion of differing lengths.
